subject.title: fix: allow trusted host-read html after outbound staging

question: Should OpenClaw accept content-bound SQLite provenance as the supported trust boundary for outbound-staged generated HTML host reads?
rationale: The patch fixes a real message-loss regression, but it deliberately extends a local HTML host-read security boundary and stores trust provenance in shared SQLite state, which needs owner intent rather than automated repair.

options.title: Accept Provenance Lifecycle
options.body: Accept the sha256+size SQLite provenance design after the branch is made mergeable, treating fail-closed DB behavior as the supported safety tradeoff.

options.title: Require A Narrower Boundary
options.body: Ask for a revised design that avoids persistent trust state or changes cleanup/failure ownership before landing.

options.title: Keep Staged HTML Blocked
options.body: Pause or close this fix path and continue requiring users to avoid generated HTML staging or convert to another document format.

recommendation.title: Accept Provenance Lifecycle
recommendation.body: Accept the sha256+size SQLite provenance design after the branch is made mergeable, treating fail-closed DB behavior as the supported safety tradeoff.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete authored and merged the original trusted generated HTML boundary and is the strongest identified owner for accepting or rejecting this lifecycle.
